name: Mixpanel
summary: Product analytics from a Mixpanel project: saved Insights reports, retention, event and property counts, user profiles and cohorts, and raw event export.

region.description: Query API server for the project's data residency: mixpanel (US), eu.mixpanel (EU) or in.mixpanel (India).

export_server.description: Raw export server for the same residency: data (US), data-eu (EU) or data-in (India).

username.description: a Mixpanel service account's username (Organization settings > Service Accounts), granted the project to read

secret.description: that service account's secret, the Basic auth password

notes: Every call needs project_id (the number in the project's settings and URL); a project with data views also needs the global view's workspace_id.
Rate limits are tight: the Query API allows 60 queries per hour and 5 concurrent per project; raw export allows 60 per hour, 3 per second and 100 concurrent. 429 when exceeded.
Dates are yyyy-mm-dd and inclusive at both ends. Query results use the project's timezone; raw export reads dates as UTC for projects created from 2023.

Several inputs are JSON encoded into one string: event lists ('["signup","purchase"]'), distinct_ids, values and filter_by_cohort. Filters (where, born_where, on) use Mixpanel's segmentation expression syntax, e.g. properties["$os"]=="Linux".
The region and export_server settings must name the same residency as the project; a project only answers on its own servers.

endpoints.name: Get a saved Insights report
endpoints.summary: The computed series of a saved Insights report, as the web app shows it.

workspace_id.description: The data view's workspace id, for projects with data views.

bookmark_id.description: The report's id: the number after 'report-' in the report's URL.

notes: series maps each metric to {date: value}; headers says what the nested keys mean.

endpoints.name: Query retention
endpoints.summary: First-time (birth) or recurring (compounded) retention cohorts over a date range, by day, week or month.

workspace_id.description: The data view's workspace id, for projects with data views.

born_event.description: The event that puts a user in a cohort. Required for birth retention.

event.description: The returning event; any event when omitted.

born_where.description: Segmentation expression filtering the born events.

interval.description: Units per bucket (default 1; at most 90 when unit is day).

interval_count.description: Number of buckets returned (default 1), plus a 0th bucket.

unbounded_retention.description: true counts a user retained on day N if they returned on day N or any later day.

on.description: Property expression to segment the returning event by.

limit.description: Top segment values to return; only with on.

endpoints.name: Count events over time
endpoints.summary: Total, unique or average counts of one or more events per minute, hour, day, week or month.

workspace_id.description: The data view's workspace id, for projects with data views.

event.description: A JSON array of event names, as one string.

unit.description: Granularity. Hourly uniques are not available.

interval.description: Number of units back from now (1 is the current unit). Give interval or from_date and to_date.

from_date.description: yyyy-mm-dd, inclusive. The reference marks it required; interval can stand in for the date pair.

endpoints.name: List today's top events
endpoints.summary: Today's most frequent events with counts and the change from yesterday.

workspace_id.description: The data view's workspace id, for projects with data views.

limit.description: Most events to return; 100 when omitted.

endpoints.name: Break an event down by a property
endpoints.summary: Counts of one event per value of one property, over time.

workspace_id.description: The data view's workspace id, for projects with data views.

name.description: The property to break down by.

values.description: A JSON array of the property values wanted, as one string; all values when omitted.

interval.description: Number of units back from now. Give interval or from_date and to_date.

limit.description: Most property values to return; 255 when omitted.

endpoints.name: Query user or group profiles
endpoints.summary: Profiles matching a filter, a cohort or a list of distinct ids, with chosen properties.

workspace_id.description: The data view's workspace id, for projects with data views.

distinct_ids.description: A JSON array of distinct ids, as one string.

data_group_id.description: A group key's id, to read group profiles instead of users.

output_properties.description: A JSON array of the property names to return, as one string. Much faster than returning every property.

filter_by_cohort.description: A JSON object {"id": <cohort id>}, as one string. Not with behaviors.

include_all_users.description: With filter_by_cohort: true (default) includes ids without a profile, false only those with one.

behaviors.description: Event selector for exporting profiles by behaviour; not with filter_by_cohort.

as_of_timestamp.description: Unix time pinning a behaviors query; needed to page past 1,000 profiles with behaviors.

session_id.description: The session_id from the previous page's answer; required for any page above 0.

notes: A POST that only reads profiles; the body is form encoded.
Pages hold up to page_size (1,000) profiles: send the first answer's session_id with page 1, 2, ... until a page comes back short.

endpoints.name: List saved cohorts
endpoints.summary: Every cohort in the project with its id, name, size, description and creation date.

workspace_id.description: The data view's workspace id, for projects with data views.

notes: A POST that only lists cohorts. To get a cohort's members, query profiles with filter_by_cohort.

endpoints.name: Get users' event activity
endpoints.summary: The event stream of one or more users over a date range.

workspace_id.description: The data view's workspace id, for projects with data views.

distinct_ids.description: A JSON array of distinct ids, as one string.

notes: Mixpanel has put this endpoint in maintenance mode.

endpoints.name: Export raw events
endpoints.summary: Raw events with every property and timestamp over a date range, optionally filtered by event name or expression.

from_date.description: yyyy-mm-dd, inclusive (UTC for projects created from 2023, else the project timezone).

limit.description: Most events to return, up to 100,000.

event.description: A JSON array of event names, as one string.

time_in_ms.description: true for millisecond timestamps; seconds by default.

notes: The answer is newline-delimited JSON, one event per line, not a JSON array. Keep the date range and limit small: a busy project's day can be gigabytes.
Goes to the export server (export_server setting), not the Query API host.
